Myocarditis: The patient presents with intermittent, sharp, central chest pain with diaphoresis, elevated troponin levels, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement on CMR, which are consistent with myocardial inflammation. The presence of mild systolic dysfunction and hypokinesia of the anterolateral and inferolateral segments on CMR further supports this diagnosis.
Myopericarditis: The patient has pleuritic chest pain worsened when sitting forward, stage 2 finger clubbing, and extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement in a mid-wall to epicardial distribution on CMR, which are indicative of myopericarditis. However, the absence of pericardial enhancement or effusion on CMR makes this diagnosis less likely than myocarditis.
